clue.text: Fast cars tail leading models

indicators.note: to tail is to follow behind, so the fast cars come after the word for leading

parts.note: arch- means chief or leading, as in arch-enemy
E-types are Jaguar sports cars of the 1960s

explanation.surface: Sports cars following behind the cars of top fashion models in a procession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail' is a verb here, meaning follow, so the cars come second. The Jaguar E-type is a classic British sports car of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Archetypes are original patterns or perfect examples that others copy, which is what a model is.

clue.text: Mayor's place at chilly ground

indicators.note: ground is the past participle of grind, so the letters are crushed and remade

explanation.surface: The mayor's home is a spot on frosty ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A city hall is the building where a mayor and council run a town's affairs.

clue.text: English declare property that's left

parts.note: to state something is to declare it

explanation.surface: An Englishman formally declares what possessions remain after a death.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's estate is everything they own, and the term is used above all for what a dead person leaves behind.

clue.text: Thug hit it off, short of time

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so one letter is removed from the phrase

parts.note: two people who hit it off got on well

explanation.surface: A heavy got along well with someone, though in too little time.
explanation.definitionFit: A goon is a hired heavy or ruffian, a slang word for a thug.

clue.text: Angles for some writer's tirades about fighter

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the writer's tirades go round the fighter

parts.note: the writer of a clue calls themself I, so writer's is I'M, short for I am
rants are angry tirades
a MiG is a Russian fighter plane

explanation.surface: A writer rants about some fighter jet, from certain angles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angles' looks like a geometric term but is the Germanic tribe that settled in England; 'about' puts the fighter inside the writer's tirades.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angles came to Britain from the Continent, so they are one example of people who settled in a new land.

clue.text: Suspect image of sweaty old fellow in mine

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the sweaty old fellow goes into the mine

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
hot means heated and perspiring

explanation.surface: A picture of a perspiring elderly man working underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A Photofit is a likeness of a wanted person put together from witness descriptions, so a police picture of a suspect.

clue.text: Hit right, then right again, in contested set

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the two rights go into the shuffled set
contested suggests something fought over and thrown into disorder

parts.note: OK is another word for all right, a second sense of right

explanation.surface: A tennis player strikes a forehand, then another, in a hard-fought set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contested' turns SET into STE, which holds R and OK.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroke is a blow or a hit, and in sport any shot played at the ball.

clue.text: You won't go far with this sort of note

definitions.text: You won't go far with this sort of note

parts.words: You won't go far with this sort of note
parts.note: a note pitched slightly low is out of tune, and a punctured tyre stops a car

explanation.surface: A warning that a certain kind of letter or banknote will get you nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is both a musical note sung under pitch and, unspoken, a tyre without air.
explanation.definitionFit: A note below pitch is called flat, and a deflated tyre of the same name ends a journey quickly.

clue.text: Feature of depression: mental aberration, scratching head

indicators.note: scratching means removing, so the first letter of the word goes

parts.note: a brainstorm is a sudden fit of mental confusion

explanation.surface: A symptom of clinical depression is a lapse of reason, with patients scratching their heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' is not the mood disorder but a weather system of low pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Atmospheric depressions bring wet, stormy weather, so a downpour is typical of one.

clue.text: Guy nicks books left in temporary accommodation

indicators.note: nicks means steals or takes in, so the guy holds the books

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a guy
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A man steals books that were left in a short-term lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: Guests stay in a hotel only for a few nights, so it is lodging for a short while.

clue.text: Cart horse takes a circuitous way home

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

indicators.note: circuitous means roundabout, so the letters take a winding course

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A carthorse wanders a roundabout route back to its stable.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hay Wain is also John Constable's famous painting, part of the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A hay wain is a farm wagon for carrying hay, a kind of cart.

clue.text: Hymn popular trio played with tenor

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: played suggests a piece performed with free variation, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: A well-loved three-piece band performs with a tenor singer.
explanation.definitionFit: An introit is the psalm or chant sung as the priest enters at the start of Mass.

clue.text: Find eastern wagon heading west

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means reading from right to left

parts.note: a cart is a wagon

explanation.surface: Locating an oriental covered wagon travelling west across the plains.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace a lost item or person is to track it down and locate it.

clue.text: Firm friend worried about large area for cropping

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled friend goes round the large letter
worried means troubled and shaken up, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A loyal friend frets over a big area that has been cut back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' turns FRIEND into RNFIED, which holds L. Constable painted The Cornfield, part of the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Cropping here means growing and harvesting crops, which is what a field of grain is used for.

clue.text: Rooster busy with grain, fabulous creature

parts.note: a cock is a rooster
at, as in at work or at it, means busy
rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A cockerel pecking away at grain, a marvellous bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabulous' means belonging to fable rather than wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockatrice is a mythical serpent hatched from a cock's egg, whose glance could kill.

clue.text: Dicky replaces this medic and resists changes around hospital

parts.note: DR is short for doctor, a medic

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the hospital letter
changes means alters, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A man named Dicky stands in for a doctor who refuses to swap clothes in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' turns RESISTS into ESSSIRT, with H placed inside. A dicky is a detachable false shirt front.
explanation.definitionFit: A dicky is worn under a jacket in place of a full formal garment, giving the look of a starched front.

clue.text: Bobby cut round symbols covering church altar for one

indicators.note: round means turned about, so the word for cut reads backwards

parts.note: to lop is to cut off

indicators.note: covering means enclosing, so the symbols wrap round the church

parts.note: icons are symbols, as on a screen
CE is the Church of England
an altar is one example of a table, the communion table

explanation.surface: A boy named Bobby trims around religious images that hide a church altar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bobby' looks like a name but is the British slang for a police officer, after Sir Robert Peel.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobby is British slang for a uniformed officer of the police, named after Robert Peel.

clue.text: Colouring stick involves tedious repetition

indicators.note: involves means wraps up or contains, so the stick holds the repetition

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
rote is mechanical learning by repetition

explanation.surface: Painting a stick is dull, repetitive work.
explanation.definitionFit: Carotene is the orange pigment that gives carrots their colour, so it is a natural colouring.

clue.text: Patient is introduced to barmy sect

indicators.note: introduced to means put inside, so the patient goes into the barmy word

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy or barmy

explanation.surface: A sick person meets a crazy religious group.
explanation.definitionFit: The Baptists are a Protestant denomination practising adult baptism, a religious group or sect.

clue.text: Special more costly modified racers?

parts.note: prices that are up have risen, so are more costly

indicators.note: modified means altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A query whether souped-up, pricier racing machines are anything special.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and description: 'modified' turns RACERS into ERCARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Supercars are expensive, high-performance sports cars, often tuned for racing speed.

clue.text: Cutter needed for each catching fish

indicators.note: catching means holding inside, so the word for each holds the fish

parts.note: per means for each, as in per head
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: An angler needs a knife for every fish caught.
explanation.walkthrough: PEELER is also old slang for a police officer, after Robert Peel, fitting the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A peeler is a kitchen tool that cuts the skin off fruit and vegetables.

clue.text: Heads Catholic primates

parts.note: apes are primates

explanation.surface: Leading Catholic archbishops, the primates of the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primates' suggests senior bishops but means apes.
explanation.definitionFit: A head is a headland jutting into the sea, another name for a cape.

clue.text: Conductor first to condemn Placido's opening in short opera

indicators.note: first to picks the opening letter of the word condemn
in means placed inside, so the opening letter goes into the shortened opera
short means cut off at the end, so the last letter is dropped
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A conductor is the first to criticise Placido Domingo's opening night in a brief opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conductor' looks musical but means a metal that carries electricity. COPPER is also slang for a police officer, fitting the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is an excellent electrical conductor, used in most household wiring.

clue.text: More agile navy leads to embarrassing row

parts.note: a fleet is a navy's ships

indicators.note: leads are the first letters, so the two words give their initials

explanation.surface: A faster navy brings on an awkward diplomatic quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleet as an adjective means swift and nimble, so its comparative means quicker and nimbler.

clue.text: Measure pay

definitions.meaning: a unit of length of twelve inches

explanation.surface: Measure the wages.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both an imperial unit of length and a verb for settling a bill.

clue.text: Work quietly among cast in camp

indicators.note: among means placed inside, so the work and quiet go into the casting word

parts.note: to cast a line is to fish
OP is short for opus, a work
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: Getting on with a job quietly among the actors at a holiday camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like a theatre company but is the verb of angling; 'camp' means theatrically affected.
explanation.definitionFit: Camp describes exaggerated, affected behaviour, much like a dandy's vain and showy manner.

clue.text: Cross France or Germany

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: Pass through either France or Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: Flatford, the mill Constable painted, ties FORD to the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To ford a river is to cross it by wading through a shallow place.

clue.text: Old tin containing energy drink

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the tin holds the energy

parts.note: a can is a tin
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: An aged can holding an energy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drink' is not a beverage but slang for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink is informal slang for the sea, as when something falls in it.

clue.text: Saw expert writer stopping president once

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the writer fills the inside of the president

parts.note: Jimmy Carter was a former US president
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An expert observer saw a writer interrupting a past president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see, but is the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodworker is skilled with a saw and other hand tools for shaping timber.
